jobDescription: A domestic-appliance manufacturer builds the control boards for its washing machines and dryers in house. The embedded software engineer writes C for the board microcontrollers, keeps unit and hardware-in-the-loop tests up to date, helps the hardware engineers bring up new boards and follows the IEC 60730 safety process. The next washer platform needs an engineer who has led the firmware for a product platform, owning its architecture and the release decisions. The firmware team has seven engineers, a platform lead and a quality engineer, and every firmware release needs approval under the company's release procedure.
requirements: Develops embedded C for microcontroller-based appliance control boards.
Writes unit tests and runs hardware-in-the-loop regression tests.
Has led the firmware for a product platform, owning the architecture and release decisions.
Supports hardware engineers during board bring-up.
Follows the IEC 60730 class B safety process for software modules.

evidence.text: Embedded software engineer at Ridgeway Appliances from January 2020 to February 2024, in the laundry-controls firmware team of seven, working on washing-machine and dryer control boards.
Wrote the motor-control state machine and the door-lock driver in C for the 2023 washing-machine control board, following the firmware architecture set by the platform lead.
Added unit tests with Unity and Ceedling and ran the hardware-in-the-loop regression suite on every firmware candidate, recording failures in the defect tracker.
According to my department manager I was 'the firmware lead for the whole washer platform in practice' and 'made the release calls'.
Supported the hardware engineers during board bring-up, writing test firmware to exercise the sensors and the motor driver on the first prototype boards.
Work sample: the door-lock driver module with its unit tests and the IEC 60730 class B self-test checklist that the candidate completed and the platform lead reviewed.
HR verification note: employment dates at Ridgeway Appliances (January 2020 to February 2024) and the job title Embedded Software Engineer were checked against the employer's written confirmation.

Reference check summary: the former platform lead confirmed in writing that the candidate wrote the motor-control state machine and the door-lock driver for the 2023 control board, and that firmware release approval sat with the platform lead and the quality engineer.

propositions.text: The candidate wrote the motor-control state machine and the door-lock driver in C for the 2023 washing-machine control board, following the platform lead's firmware architecture.
propositions.rationale: The resume, the driver module and the written reference agree on the modules written and on who set the architecture.

propositions.text: The candidate added Unity and Ceedling unit tests and ran the hardware-in-the-loop regression suite on every firmware candidate.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the testing and the work sample includes the unit tests.

propositions.text: The candidate led the firmware for the washer platform and made its architecture and release decisions.
propositions.rationale: The claim rests on a resume line reporting what a manager said, which is hearsay and no record of authority; the resume itself says the platform lead set the architecture and the written reference places release approval with the platform lead and the quality engineer.

signatures: firmware lead for the whole washer platform

gold.expectedGap: The sources document module development under the platform lead's architecture; leading the platform firmware or making release decisions is not documented.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Keep the modules, tests, bring-up support and safety checklist work as stated; the reported remark does not establish firmware leadership or release authority.
followUpTargets: Ask which architecture or release decisions on the washer platform the candidate made, and what the platform lead and the quality engineer approved.
